defects: (a) THE SEAT'S: A READ-FIRST BANK THAT QUOTED AN OLD PRINT IN THE COMPILER'S FORM. data/b654_readfirst.txt quoted b557's print of the T3 terminal line for line, quotes and all; tools/axiom_claim.py reads every tracked data bank carrying a print line and lets the latest act's bank stand, and the read-first sorts after the re-banked print, so G-AXIOM-CLAIM's first run after the re-bank still read the claim at AxiomCheck.lean:8 CONTRADICTED, its source the read-first. Caught on that run, before the face; the quote rewritten outside the compiler's line form in a correction commit, and every b654 bank searched for the form.

(b) THE NAVIGATOR'S, ON THE AUTHOR'S WORD: AN EXPECTATION THAT OMITTED THE STANDING WORKFLOW FILE. N5 read "no kernel main written except the merge under Component 4", and SIDE-explicit-formula carried no workflow on its main, so the one dispatch (R264)(3) orders could not be made without writing that main. Put to the author at Component 2 before any Lean; the author's answer: (R263)(4) is the standing form, a kernel repository a branch touches carries the workflow file on its main, dispatched by hand; the file written on SIDE-explicit-formula's main under that clause; N5 reads from here "no kernel main written except the workflow file under (R263)(4) and the merge under Component 4" -- the navigator's omission.

(c) THE SEAT'S: A RECURSIVE GREP OVER A KERNEL'S PACKAGE TREE. Looking for a core lemma's name, the seat ran a recursive grep over SIDE-explicit-formula's .lake tree in place of git grep in the package's own repository; it ran past the 120 s foreground limit and went to the background. The task was stopped, and its two children were left running (grep, PID 32200, the recursive search; head, PID 14116), each stopped by PID with its command line printed; the process list then read 0. Nothing was written. The name was then sought with git grep alone.

(d) THE SEAT'S: TWO REMOTE BRANCH DELETES WRITTEN WITH A REDIRECT. At step zero the merged work branches were deleted at the remote by `git push origin --delete <name>` with the push's output redirected to a bank in the same command (relay data/b654_commands.txt #22, #23); tools/edit_route.py reads every word after the remote as a branch name, the redirect and its target among them, and reads both commands as branch deletions without an explicit name. Each command named its one branch, and the branch lists read 0 after it; but the house form is the delete alone, so G-EDIT-ROUTE fails on the act's capture as it stands. It is declared on the face; the capture is not edited.

(b) the navigator's, on the author's word: an expectation that omitted the standing workflow file
(c) the seat's: a recursive grep over a kernel's package tree
(d) the seat's: two remote branch deletes written with a redirect
